cards.title: Five statuses
cards.text: Same model as Delve: each hit builds up to 100, then something bigger happens.
cards.why: Delve's statuses already work this way, so it's tested. Mark any part that's off.

parts.title: Burn → Flare
parts.text: Damage over time. At 100 it drops to 20, a big hit, and a small fire blast that burns those nearby.

parts.title: Chill → Freeze → Shatter
parts.text: Slows up to 60%. At 100: frozen 2 s. A hard hit on a frozen enemy shatters it into icicles that chill others.

parts.title: Shock → Overload
parts.text: Each hit arcs a small jump to one nearby enemy. At 100: stunned 0.6 s and arcs to 3.

parts.title: Poison → Rot
parts.text: Slow damage. At 100: loses 15% of max HP at once. Dies leaving a gas cloud that poisons.

parts.title: Mark → Detonate
parts.text: No damage. Marked enemies take +25% from your hits. At 5 marks it pops for heavy damage.

parts.title: Three mixes
parts.text: Thaw: Burn on chill clears both for a burst. Ignite: fire in gas explodes. Conduct: Shock arcs prefer marked enemies and jump twice as far between them.

parts.title: Hard effects
parts.text: Knockback, stun (from Freeze and Overload) and slow (from Chill). These don't build up.

cards.title: Beams build slower
cards.text: Beams and trails add less build-up per tick than a bolt hit?
cards.why: A beam ticks 8 times a second. At full strength, Burn on a beam would Flare everything instantly and other shapes would never be worth it.
cards.pick: Yes: each shape has a strength for statuses; beams and trails are low, the Ball and charged shots are high.

cards.title: Enemies use statuses
cards.text: Elite enemies can burn, chill or shock you?
cards.why: Elites carry modules (see Enemies), so an elite with Burn would set you on fire. It keeps one system both ways. The cost: you need a way to shake statuses off.
cards.pick: Yes, from elites only; a dash clears half your build-up.
